tagline: Here the college came first and the town followed.
intro: The ride starts at the county line on Davidson's Main Street, part of the old trade route between Charlotte and Statesville, runs south past the college, then turns out Concord Road into the Piedmont and ends at Fisher Farm Park. It is 5.5 miles.

Presbyterian farmers founded the college in 1837 and the town grew up around it, answering to the name Davidson College until 1891. Beyond the last houses come farmhouses, barns and pasture, and on weekends the bicycles. The state guidebook, citing local bike shops, put it at 60 to 300 riders a weekend.

moments.title: Davidson College
moments.text: An arboretum begun in 1869 covers the whole campus, and Oak and Elm Rows, built as dormitories, later sheltered Confederate soldiers on their way home.

moments.title: Helper Hotel
moments.text: Across Main Street from the campus, a building of 1848 that opened as a store and soon went over to putting up college visitors.

moments.title: Concord Road marker
moments.text: A campus marker remembers physics professor Henry Louis Smith and his X-ray work with his students in 1896, among the first in America.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, The College Town Ride
